instantiated_cells.justification: State agencies do not register as principals/lobbyists under §13.64; instead each agency files a separate statement under §13.695 identifying employees who attempt to influence legislative action, and §13.621(2) exempts such agencies from §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, and 13.68.
The Governor is an "elective state official" (§13.62(6)) and per §13.621(3) elective state officials acting in official capacity are not subject to §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, or 13.695.

Independent agencies fall within the broad "agency" definition in §13.62(2) and file under §13.695 rather than registering as principals, and §13.621(2) exempts them from the standard licensing/registration provisions.
§13.621(1)(d) provides a complete exemption from the subchapter for "lobbying of an agency official by an agency official of a different agency or another agency official of the same agency."
§13.621(3) provides that an employee of the legislature is not subject to §§13.63, 13.64, 13.65, 13.68, or 13.695 when acting in an official capacity.

A lobbying firm that employs lobbyists falls within the definition of "principal" (§13.62(12) — any person who employs a lobbyist) and must register under §13.64 if expenditures exceed $500; the firm's individual lobbyists must also be licensed under §13.63.

The statute repeatedly references "a principal that is a local governmental unit" in §13.625(4m)(e) and (f), indicating local governments can be principals subject to registration under §13.64; the §13.621(3) exemption applies only to individual local officials acting in official capacity, not to the local government as a principal employing lobbyists.
§13.63(1)(a) requires lobbyists to obtain a license from the commission, and §13.66 prohibits engaging in lobbying as a lobbyist unless licensed under §13.63 and authorized under §13.65.
§13.64(1) requires every principal who makes lobbying expenditures or incurs obligations exceeding $500 in a calendar year to file a registration statement with the commission within 10 days.

"Principal" under §13.62(12) means "any person" who employs a lobbyist, with no exclusion for non-agency public entities; such entities must register under §13.64 if exceeding the $500 threshold, since only state agencies (§13.621(2)) and individual officials acting officially (§13.621(3)) are exempted.

The definition of "lobbyist" in §13.62(11) requires the individual to be employed by a principal or to contract for/receive economic consideration (other than reimbursement of actual expenses), so unpaid volunteer lobbyists fall outside the definition and are not required to be licensed; §13.68(1)(c) further references "unpaid volunteer" time as excludable.

content.text:
I'll analyze each entity type against the Wisconsin lobbying statute to determine registration requirements.

Key statutory framework:
- §13.63: Lobbyists must obtain a license
- §13.64: Principals (who employ lobbyists) exceeding $500 must register
- §13.65: Lobbyist authorization must be filed
- §13.62(11): Lobbyist definition requires economic consideration (excludes pure volunteers)
- §13.62(12): "Principal" means any person who employs a lobbyist
- §13.621(3): Elective state officials/local officials/tribal officials/legislative employees acting in official capacity are exempt
- §13.621(1)(d): Agency-to-agency lobbying is completely exempt
- §13.695: State agencies file a separate statement (not the standard registration)
